evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the information the user needs to provide (name and optional description) rather than prescribing a concrete UI widget or implementation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete invitation mechanism (providing a URL) rather than only stating the need to invite estimators.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget (single multi-line text field) instead of the underlying need to supply an item to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States a stakeholder need (visibility of all items) without prescribing UI widgets or technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the goal/action (select an item) without prescribing concrete UI controls or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the stakeholder need to add items without prescribing how the UI or storage should be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to edit items rather than mandating particular UI widgets or implementation approaches.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to remove items without prescribing technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired behavior (show estimates immediately) but does not prescribe specific UI widgets or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete aggregation algorithm (average) as the way to accept estimates, which is a solution choice rather than the stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes an automatic field-filling behavior and ties it to a specific UI concept ('estimate' field, cards) - an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the need to record the agreed estimate without mandating UI widgets or internal mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Describes the stakeholder need (re-estimate) and does not prescribe implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete data interchange mechanism/format (spreadsheet import) rather than simply stating the need to bulk-add stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific interaction and source format (copy/paste from spreadsheet) which is a solution-level detail.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to find prior games without prescribing UI controls or storage mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States a stakeholder need (view transcript) without specifying implementation or file formats.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies an export format (HTML file), which is a concrete solution choice rather than the underlying need to save transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete export/storage format (CSV), which is an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States the need to remove stored data without prescribing how deletion or storage should be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Lists required account information (what the user must provide) rather than prescribing specific UI widgets or internal mechanisms; treated as stakeholder data needs.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific authentication mechanism (account name and password) rather than stating the general need to authenticate.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the stakeholder need to update account information without mandating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: States a data-retention/removal need without prescribing technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a user-visible requirement (local timezone) without prescribing the mechanism for timezone conversion.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete communication mechanism (email) for password reminders instead of the higher-level need to recover access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific estimation scales (concrete solution choices) rather than only stating the need to choose an estimate scale.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Provides a stakeholder requirement (maximum number of participants) but does not mandate implementation or UI details.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Describes a specific joining mechanism (enter name on a page accessed via URL) rather than the general need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States a visibility need for the estimator without prescribing UI widgets or technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user need to view session items without specifying implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes the desired visibility/feedback but does not prescribe specific UI widgets or mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the timing of showing estimates (simultaneous after all input) which is a behavior requirement, not a low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Defines a rule for when estimates may change (a business rule) rather than prescribing UI widgets or implementation mechanics.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the informational need to view prior estimates without mandating how this is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States a visibility need (who gave what) without prescribing UI controls or internal structures.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete UI/feature implementation (a visible two-minute countdown timer) rather than the higher-level need to limit discussion time.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific behavior of a concrete solution (automatic timer reset at a particular event) instead of stating the underlying need.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Uses a concrete UI interaction ('scroll back') to describe navigation; this prescribes a solution-level interaction rather than purely stating the navigation need.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired consistent behavior (ordering) relevant to the user experience, not a low-level UI widget or technical mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Defines a business rule about when estimates can be changed rather than prescribing specific UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete UI details (a small thumbnail displayed near cards), which is a solution-level presentation choice.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technical standards (XHTML/CSS compliance) which are implementation/technical choices rather than a pure stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States the need for shared definitions/documentation without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: Explicitly prescribes an implementation detail (database indexes) rather than expressing the performance need alone.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete implementation/compatibility targets (exact browser versions), which is a technical choice instead of a pure stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes compliance with a specific technical standard (W3C guidelines) which is an implementation-level requirement.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a non-functional stakeholder need (responsiveness) without prescribing how that performance is achieved.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a user need (support for any language); although it implies a technical encoding, it is a clear stakeholder requirement rather than an unnecessary internal implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user-facing requirement about URL behavior and predictability without mandating implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: States a UX quality need (friendly error pages) without prescribing specific implementation techniques.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) which reflects a stakeholder need for anonymity rather than an unnecessary low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to view usage metrics without prescribing how metrics are collected or stored.
